newsitem.title: USA: December IMM marks, yen and Swiss finish lower.
newsitem.headline: December IMM marks, yen and Swiss finish lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mixed in quiet afternoon trading, with December marks, yen and Swiss francs in the bottom half of their daily ranges.
December marks slumped to a fresh contract low at $0.6494 near midday, under pressure from news Russian security chief Alexander Lebed was sacked by President Boris Yeltsin.
December yen got hit near the close by selling from a U.S. bank, traders said, taking the contract near day session lows.
"You saw a lot of (selling) late and the dollar's a little stronger, but we didn't make any new ground," an IMM trader said.
December yen settled down $0.000002 at $0.008980, near the day session low but up from the contract low set Wednesday and matched overnight at $0.008972.
December sterling was buoyed by higher oil prices and by perceptions it was a safe-haven currency for European Monetary Union concerns.
Traders maintained an upside target of $1.60 for the contract, and said sterling appeared to be pausing after reaching a contract high earlier this week.
After four sessions of steep losses, Mexican pesos rebounded from early September levels, closing higher.
They said players who got short on the decline took profits. Aggressive size buyers were noted at $0.124000 and at $0.124200.
December Canadian dollar finished higher, with volume strong there earlier in the day, traders said. Resistance in December was seen at $0.7431, $0.7444 and $0.7450.
"Those are targets but we need to close above $0.7430 soon," an IMM trader said.
A flurry of U.S. data had scant effect on currency futures, traders said.
September housing starts fell 6.0 percent to a 1.438 million annual rate and August starts were revised to up 4.0 percent. Jobless claims rose to 340,000 in the Oct 12 week.
U.S. September industrial output rose 0.2 percent compared with an 0.4 percent rise in August. Capacity utilization was at 83.3 percent versus 83.4 percent in August.
The Philadelphia Federal Reserve Bank's diffusion index fell to 5.3 in October from 13.9 in September. The prices-paid index rose to 21.9 from 18.0 in September.

At settlement, marks were down $0.0019 to $0.6504, Swiss francs were off $0.0016 to $0.7923, sterling rose $0.0022 to $1.5852, Canada's dollar was up $0.0012 to $0.7418, Australian dollar was up $0.0015 to $0.7911 and the peso was up $0.001625 to $0.124825.
